text: This secondary slice owns no legacy criterion of RWB-E1-057. It answers the partner half of legacy AC2 (Partner SFTP) and of legacy AC7 (An unknown or suspended partner is refused) at component level, and it writes ten criteria of its own tagged (new, D-RCV-60) that test only the partner read. The eleven criteria the split plan gives RWB-P5-E1057-APP stay there and the end-to-end proof of the two partner criteria rests with RWB-P5-E1057-APP and RWB-ITG-E1057-ITG.
why: The split plan gives this slice an empty acs list, and Template and Rules R7.2 and WP item 4 ask a story without owned legacy criteria to write criteria that test only its own deliverable rather than to copy a criterion whose deliverable is another service's. The P5 slice states in its sections 1, 7, 16 and 19 that the five criteria are proved by RWB-S9-E1057-APP, so the partner half is stated here and the ownership stays with the plan; copying the five criteria would claim a document_intake row this service never writes.
read: Split plan slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP (acs [], secondary true, C RWB-P5-E1057-CON); RWB-P5-E1057-APP sections 1, 5, 7, 16 and 19; RWB-ITG-E1057-ITG fragment (the five legacy criteria as an ITG copy); legacy RWB-E1-057 AC2, AC7 and section 12; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 and R9
confirm: Programme lead and the rwb-document and rwb-partner tech leads, from the wave 1 planning gate
impact: One owner per legacy criterion in the registers: the eleven of P5 stay there, the partner half is answered here, and the trace of legacy AC2 and AC7 runs through this read without a second claim

text: The legacy in-process PartnerDirectory.findByCode becomes one read of rwb-partner on the published GET /partners (API-S9-001) with one additive optional code filter, under base /api/recovery/partner/v1, partner-portal right R with the scope applied, one hop and a 2 s budget with a breaker, faked in the build. No second path, no new operation and no new element is declared. A code that resolves to no partner answers 200 with an empty list, because that operation publishes 401, 403 and 503 and no not-found error.
why: The six published operations of the service list partners with panel status and score under GET /partners and none of them reads a partner by code, while DP-11 turns the legacy in-process interface into a published REST read. Adding a path or an operation would widen the published surface of the service without a source, and answering 404 would declare an error that T-A.2 does not publish; the filter and the empty list are the smallest change that keeps major version 1.
read: TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2; context pack ownership rows (6 REST operations) and service row (base /api/recovery/partner/v1); legacy RWB-E1-057 section 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13, ADR-020
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-partner tech lead, before the contract is tagged
impact: One additive query parameter on a published operation, no new path, no new element and no not-found error, and the intake builds against the fake from Day 1

text: The answer carries exactly the six published properties of a partner - id, partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status and score - and no reason property. The panel decision stays with the caller: a row with panel_status ACTIVE takes the file in, any other stored status is refused with the legacy reason PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE and an empty list with PARTNER_UNKNOWN, and both reasons are rendered by the intake in its own MSG-P5-007.
why: The published Partner element and TSD S9 T3.1 give those six fields and no reason, and the two reasons are values of the intake job record of legacy AC7 with no published code list. A reason property would add a business value and an element the service does not own; keeping BR4 in the caller executes the rule once and leaves the panel data with its owner.
read: TSD S9 T3.1 (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007) and T3.2; legacy RWB-E1-057 AC7, BR4 and section 12; FSD S9 A2.1.3.2 and A2.2.3.1; context pack ownership rows (table partner)
confirm: Business lead and the rwb-document tech lead, before wave 1 starts
impact: The panel rule is executed in one place, the answer stays inside the published element and no refusal text is duplicated between the two services

text: The nine patterns of the key are carried in the metadata because they are the key's, and four of them take effect outside this read: DP-06 lands in RWB-P5-E1057-APP for the five INTAKE_* parameter rows, DP-09 in the instruction steps that publish EV-20 and EV-21, DP-10 in the intake Schedule of rwb-document and DP-19 in the partner portal stories. DP-07 adds the client library RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (H) and the reference-data row RWB-P3-E1043-CON (C), and those two rows are stated in sections 12.2 and 13 but are not carried in the metadata, because the split plan gives this secondary slice an empty H row; DP-01, DP-11, DP-13 and DP-15 add nothing.
why: Template and Rules R5.5 gives each pattern its added dependency and WP item 1 asks the H row to be copied from the plan, which is empty here. Taking the DP-07 rows into the metadata would contradict the plan row, and dropping the pattern would leave the list read undocumented; the split is therefore stated, and the divergence is tracked so the row can be added centrally if the coordinator prefers it.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5, R5.7, R7.1 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP (H [], C [RWB-P5-E1057-CON], patterns DP01, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19); context pack DP table short form, service row (Jobs 0) and ownership rows; TSD S9 T5.2
confirm: Programme lead and the solutions architect, at the wave 1 planning gate
impact: The metadata keeps the plan's empty H row, the DP-07 rows are visible and traceable in the body, and a central decision adds them without rewriting the story

text: The read publishes and consumes no event. The topic rwb.partner.events.v1 with its retry and .dlt topics and the event names rwb.partner.<Event>.v1 stay this service's, and EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted belong to the instruction steps and to the portal result, so this story declares no outbox row, no producer group, no consumer group and no inbox row.
why: A read that changes nothing announces nothing, and the context pack gives the service its two events with the workflow InstructionWorkflow, not with a directory read. Declaring an event for the panel read would invent a name the catalogue does not hold and would add the outbox library dependency that DP-09 would bring.
read: Context pack ownership rows (events EV-20 and EV-21, topic rwb.partner.events.v1, workflow InstructionWorkflow) and service row; TSD S9 T5.3; legacy RWB-E1-057 section 12 (events published None); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14
confirm: Solution architect and the event owner, when the topic and event catalogue is baselined
impact: No outbox, inbox or idempotency row and no producer or consumer group for this read, and the two published events of the service stay with the instruction steps

text: The lookup on partner_code runs on the per-service Flyway baseline that creates partner in rwb_partner, and this story adds no migration, no table and no column. The name and the definition of the constraint or index that makes the lookup return one row are Not specified in the source documents and carry the placeholder; the read is written so that a second row with the same code cannot change the answer of one call.
why: TSD S9 T3.1 publishes the columns and the lists of partner and no constraint, index or key name, and DP-15 puts the schema in the service's own sequence rather than in a shared baseline. Inventing a constraint name would be a value no source holds, and leaving the lookup undefined would let a duplicate code answer two rows.
read: TSD S9 T3.0, T3.1 and T3.2; legacy RWB-E1-057 section 13 (the legacy migration of the intake columns); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15 and R9; context pack service row (schema rwb_partner)
confirm: ACE team and the rwb-partner tech lead, before the service schema is baselined
impact: The read ships with the baseline that owns the table, the constraint is named when the schema owner publishes it, and no migration is written by this story

text: No source publishes the transition table of LOV-PANEL, so this story states only the reading that BR4 needs: panel_status ACTIVE admits a partner file and every other published value - ON_NOTICE, SUSPENDED and EXITED - refuses it as PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE. No state is set by this story and the moves between panel states belong to the onboarding, panel and exit stories.
why: TSD S9 T3.2 publishes the four panel values and no transition between them, and legacy BR4 turns on ACTIVE alone. Writing moves or inventing a fifth state would be a business definition no source holds, while stating that every non-ACTIVE value refuses keeps the legacy rule exact.
read: TSD S9 T3.2 (LOV-PANEL); FSD S9 A1.2, A2.1.3.1 and A2.2.3.1; legacy RWB-E1-057 BR4 and AC7; Template and Rules v1 R9
confirm: Business lead and the panel owner, before wave 1 starts
impact: The intake admits ACTIVE only, the three other values refuse with the legacy reason, and the panel moves stay with the stories that own them

text: Wave 1 and release 30 November 2026 stay as the split plan gives them: EP01 is wave 1 and the service's Arch v5 wave is 4, so under R5.6 the earlier W-MAP wave is kept and one conflict is raised per service and business epic, and the release date is copied unchanged and marked tentative.
why: Template and Rules R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave where it is earlier than the service wave and asks for one conflict gap per service and business epic; U7 and R9 say a release date is copied, marked tentative and never raised as a gap. Choosing wave 4 would move a story out of the plan's wave and change the delivery date of the intake.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.6, R5.7, R7.1 and U7; split plan slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP (wave 1, release 30 November 2026); context pack service row (wave 4); Architecture v5 slide 4 (epics 6 and 7 for S9)
confirm: Programme lead, at the wave 1 planning gate
impact: The story keeps wave 1 and carries 30 November 2026 (tentative), and the one service and business epic conflict is recorded once for S9 and EP01

text: The story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) and is built against the Draft contract baseline RWB-P5-E1057-CON and its fake. No approval of this realigned story, of the split plan or of the intake contract is recorded in the run, so no Ready for build or Approved status is claimed and no human approval is awaited.
why: Template and Rules R7.1 fixes the status row and the run rules say a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the story continues in Draft. Claiming an approved status without a recorded approval would misstate the gate the story has passed.
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.1, R8.1 and U8; run rules for D-RCV-60 (no human approval stop, record an assumption and continue in Draft); split plan slice RWB-S9-E1057-APP (build_status Not started)
confirm: Programme lead and the quality lead, at the verification loop that follows this run
impact: The story is buildable on the Draft baseline from Day 1 and its status moves with the verification loop, not with this run
